stages.name: Implement
stages.prompt:
Implement the task below on your current working branch.

Read the task in full before changing anything. Follow its Agent notes exactly: they are decisions already made, not suggestions. Do not make a decision the task leaves open; if the task cannot be completed without one, stop, leave the tree unchanged, and say what is missing in your final message.

Change only what the task asks for. Do not add marker files, unrelated cleanups, or any file the task does not name.

Run every command under "How to check" and make each one pass before you finish. Commit on your current working branch with a clear message that names the task. Do NOT push anything. Do NOT open a pull request. Do NOT call factory update. A later stage reviews and delivers this work. Your job ends at the commit.

{{ task.prompt }}

stages.name: Review
stages.prompt:
You are reviewing work you did not write. The previous stage implemented the task below and committed it on this working branch. The commits since the target base branch are the work under review.

Inspect the work with git log and git diff against the target base branch. Run every command under "How to check" and read the results yourself. Confirm that the diff does what the task asks, that every item under "Done when" holds, that nothing outside the task changed, and that no file the task does not name was added.

Do NOT push. Do NOT open a pull request. Do NOT call factory update. Do NOT change the code: a review that edits the work is not a review. A later stage delivers.

Record your verdict by making the FIRST line of your final message exactly one of these, with nothing before it:

FACTORY-VERDICT: approve
FACTORY-VERDICT: request-changes
FACTORY-VERDICT: blocked

Use approve only if the diff does exactly what the task asks and every check passes. Use request-changes if it does not, and say precisely what is wrong. Use blocked if you cannot tell. Anything else, including no verdict line at all, means the factory will not merge. After the first line, say what you checked and what each check returned.

{{ task.prompt }}

stages.name: Deliver
stages.prompt:
Deliver the work the previous stages implemented and reviewed. Do not change any code and do not add any file.

The Factory publish branch is {{ branch }}. That exact branch is the only branch a delivery may come from.

1. Push the reviewed commits to the Factory publish branch:
   git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/{{ branch }}
2. Open a pull request against the target base branch named above FROM that publish branch:
   gh pr create --head {{ branch }} --base <the target base branch> --title "<the title>" --body-file <a file you write>
   The task name is: {{ task.name }}
   That name ends in an admission id, a space and eight hex characters in parentheses. The title is the task name with that id removed and nothing else added: no prefix, no other id.
   The body has three short parts: what changed and why, in the task's own words; how it was checked, listing each command under "How to check" and its result; and any judgment the implementer or reviewer recorded. Do not paste the task text.
3. Do NOT merge the pull request. The factory decides whether to merge it.
4. Report the outcome with factory update, using --status ready, --pr set to the pull request URL, and a concise --message.

The pull request head branch must equal the Factory publish branch or the report is refused with delivery_branch_mismatch.

{{ task.prompt }}
